title: Latency Mosaic: composite panels for model/route streaming vs non-streaming p50/p95/p99
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a composite dashboard (Latency Mosaic) that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route with an explicit streaming vs non-streaming breakdown, integrated trace links, anomaly flags from the metrics pipeline, and lightweight per-cohort sparklines. Goal is a single-pane-of-glass for oncall and SRE to rapidly judge impact and drill to traces or logs.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for selected model(s) and route(s) with a toggle for streaming vs non-streaming I/O mode.
Each latency series is annotatable with deployment rollouts and autoscaling events pulled from the events stream.
Click-through from any percentile datapoint opens a filtered trace view (trace id/time window) with pre-applied sampling rules.
Anomaly overlay (from metrics pipeline) flags windows where latency deviates beyond configured dynamic baseline.
Dashboard queries respect RBAC and load minimally on Prometheus by using pre-aggregated metrics from the metrics pipeline.
Performance: dashboard panel load time < 2s for typical 7-day window and < 4s for 30-day window in staging cluster
notes: We will rely on the new log-joiner pipeline to attach route metadata to traces for easier correlation.
Use pre-aggregated histograms exported from the runtime to reduce cardinality and Prometheus scrape cost.
Streaming vs non-streaming classification is inferred from request.io_mode tag (value: streaming|blocking) emitted by the runtime middleware.
Prefer configurable dashboard tiles so product and SRE can pin different breakdowns (per-model, per-route, per-tenant).
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Kickoff — sketched mosaic layout in Figma (linked). Decision to emphasize p95/p99 for alerts and p50 for user-facing regressions.
2026-03-11 Arjun Rao: Implemented backend histogram export and added request.io_mode tag to OTLP spans. Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721
2026-03-12 SRE Review (Priya Nair): Requested that the anomaly thresholds be configurable per-route and added guidance to avoid noisy alerts for small-volume routes.

2026-03-13 Design Feedback (Luca Moreno): Suggested compact cohort sparklines and color palette aligned with console theme. Updated Figma: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Latency+Mosaic+Design
2026-03-14 Arjun Rao: Hooked trace links to jaeger with pre-filter by model+route+time. Next: hook into rollout events stream and add event annotations.
tracing_hooks: Add a sampling hook that marks high-latency requests for full-span retention. Enrich traces with route/model tags at middleware entry and emit a correlation_id token to logs. Use OTLP batch export with low-latency flush for flagged traces.
dashboard_panels: Mosaic grid: per-model tiles with top-3 routes and p50/p95/p99 lines (streaming vs non-streaming split)
Cohort overlay: request-shape cohorts (short/med/long) with percentile ribbons
Anomaly timeline: highlighted latency anomalies with event annotations (deploys/scale/burst)
Trace jump: click a datapoint to open Jaeger/Trace UI with prefilter
Route health table: error rate, latency trend, throughput, recent anomalies
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): build panels with synthetic data and validate performance (target: 2026-03-17)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5 internal customer routes, monitor telemetry load and tune preaggregation (target: 2026-03-19)
Phase 3 (ga): enable read-only for all orgs and create runbook for oncall (target: 2026-03-21)
follow_up_tasks: Add per-tenant sampling caps to avoid trace storage spikes
Expose anomaly tuning UI in the console for SREs
Add synthetic-load tests for 30-day dashboards to measure cost
